title: Textiles, chemicals can fuel India’s aim to be manufacturing hub: Govt
content:
India’s textile industry can strengthen its global competitiveness by improving raw material availability, scaling up manufacturing through infrastructure support and expanding market access through deeper trade integration, a NITI Aayog report said. 
The chemicals sector also has the potential to enhance domestic value addition by expanding downstream production and improving feedstock utilisation.

title: India's WPI inflation eases to 9.78% in July 2026
content:
India’s WPI inflation eased to 9.78 per cent YoY in July 2026 from 9.87 per cent in June, while the all-commodities index slipped to 110.0. 
Manufactured products inflation rose to 8.29 per cent from 7.48 per cent, with its index reaching 108.4. Primary articles inflation increased to 8.52 per cent, while fuel and power inflation moderated sharply to 20.05 per cent.

title: US cotton export sales surge as new crop bookings accelerate: USDA
content:
US Upland cotton net sales for 2026-27 totalled 905,000 RB, led by Vietnam, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Mexico and India. 
Upland shipments reached 140,500 RB in the opening days of the new marketing year, with Vietnam the largest destination. 
Pima net sales stood at 50,600 RB, led by India, while USDA data signalled firm new-season demand and early-season shipments.

title: Indonesia now faces 10% US reciprocal tariff: Trade Minister Santoso
content:
US reciprocal tariff on Indonesia is 10 per cent now, the latter’s Trade Minister Budi Santoso said. 
The tariff followed a US Section 301 probe into the use of forced labour. 
After the apex US court annulled the 18-per cent reciprocal tariff initially imposed on Indonesia, a 10-per cent rate was applied to all countries for 150 days, which ended on July 24. 
Indonesia will continue to seek a lower rate.

title: South India cotton yarn remains stable, hike may hurt demand
content:
South India cotton yarn markets stayed unchanged in Tiruppur and Mumbai amid rising cotton and slow downstream demand. 
Fabric buyers and power looms cannot absorb higher yarn and cotton costs; mills may review selling rates upward mid-month. 
Gujarat cotton rose by ₹500 per candy; Shankar-6 traded at ₹68,000–68,500, with arrivals at 7,000–8,000 bales.

title: Tariff refunds: Bangladesh garment makers face a new hurdle
content:
Bangladesh garment exporters reportedly cut prices or offered discounts to retain US orders after the tariff shock, absorbing part of buyers’ higher import costs. 
US importers of record, not Bangladeshi suppliers, are in line for refunds on invalidated IEEPA duties, leaving factories reliant on negotiations. 
Relief is expected via future price hikes, larger orders or freight-cost concessions.

title: Bangladesh’s green advantage faces the profitability test
content:
Bangladesh’s 284 LEED-certified units, including 52 of the world’s top 100, keep it a green apparel manufacturing benchmark. 
Green factories can cost 20–30 per cent more upfront, yet certification does not assure higher prices, orders or bargaining power. 
With buyers widening ESG checks on traceability, emissions and resource use, makers need productivity, technology and efficiency gains.

title: Cambodia moves into the next tier of global apparel sourcing
content:
US apparel imports from Cambodia rose 15.4 per cent to $1.84 billion in the first five months of 2026.
US footwear imports from Cambodia surged 56.9 per cent to $768 million, while India’s apparel imports fell 26.0 per cent and footwear 18.5 per cent.
Cambodia has a lower US forced-labour tariff than Vietnam, comparable garment wages and no country-specific forced-labour list overhang.

title: Bangladesh takes Denim’s lead as global sourcing shifts east
content:
Bangladesh is now the single largest supplier of denim jeans to both the United States and European Union, a first for the category.
It accounted for about 26 per cent of US denim jean imports in 2025 and about 30 per cent of EU denim jean imports.
China’s US share fell from 20.3 per cent in 2019 to 6.3 per cent in 2025, reflecting structural repricing in a roughly $90 billion global.

title: How did EMEA drive US’ Brooks Running’s H1 2026 growth?
content:
Brooks Running has posted a record Q2 2026, with year-to-date revenue rising 14 per cent on strong demand for footwear, apparel and accessories. 
First-half (H1) revenue grew 9 per cent in the Americas, 39 per cent in EMEA and 10 per cent in APAC. 
Trail styles surged 71 per cent in Q2, while accessories rose 29 per cent and lifestyle footwear recorded near triple-digit growth.

title: How did Switzerland's On swing from loss to $129 mn profit in Q2 2026?
content:
On Holding AG has reported a sharp rise in net income to CHF 105.0 million (~$129.07 million, as per conversion rate of $1 = CHF0.8135 as on August 14, 2026) for Q2 2026, as net sales climbed 13.5 per cent to CHF 850.3 million (~$1.05 billion).
DTC sales surged 26 per cent, and Asia-Pacific revenue jumped 43.1 per cent, outpacing other regions.
The company raised its full 2026 outllok.

title: UK's ASOS unveils autumn campaign spotlighting fashion creativity
content:
ASOS has launched an autumn campaign centred on styling guidance and behind-the-scenes fashion content for shoppers. 
ASOS Magazine will return in September as a quarterly Substack title, with a limited print edition and cultural contributors. 
Consumer research on demand for outfit ideas backs a London Fashion Week pop-up and an autumn edit across ASOS DESIGN, Topshop and partner brands.
